medications.duration: Lifelong – review BP and renal function after 2 weeks, then annually
medications.purpose: Essential hypertension; renal and cardiovascular protection in metabolic syndrome
medications.nice_justification: NICE NG136 recommends ACE‑I as first‑line for hypertension in metabolic syndrome; CG181 endorses ACE‑I for CV risk reduction

medications.duration: Lifelong – lipid profile at 3 months, then annually
medications.purpose: Dyslipidaemia (LDL‑C 165 mg/dL) and primary CVD prevention
medications.nice_justification: NICE CG181 advises statin therapy for patients with QRISK ≥10 % or LDL‑C >100 mg/dL

medications.dose: 500 mg PO once daily with evening meal, increase by 500 mg weekly to target 1500‑2000 mg/day as tolerated
medications.duration: Lifelong – HbA1c every 3‑6 months, review renal function annually
medications.purpose: Prediabetes / insulin resistance to prevent progression to type 2 diabetes
medications.nice_justification: NICE NG28 & PH38 recommend metformin for high‑risk prediabetes

medications.dose: 0.25 mg subcutaneous weekly, titrate every 4 weeks to 1 mg (up to 2 mg if needed)

medications.nice_justification: NICE NG28/PH46 support GLP‑1 RA for obesity with metabolic disease

medications.duration: Lifelong – review renal function at 3 months then annually

interactions_checked.interaction: Additive antihypertensive effect may cause symptomatic hypotension, especially after first ramipril dose.
interactions_checked.action: Start ramipril at 2.5 mg, monitor BP and orthostatic symptoms; consider stopping thiazide once target BP achieved.

interactions_checked.interaction: ACE‑I can modestly increase atorvastatin plasma levels, raising rare myopathy risk.
interactions_checked.action: Use atorvastatin (not simvastatin); monitor CK if muscle symptoms develop.

interactions_checked.interaction: Thiazide may increase statin concentrations, especially simvastatin; effect minimal with atorvastatin.
interactions_checked.action: No dose change required; monitor for myopathy.

interactions_checked.interaction: Both increase diuresis → risk of volume depletion, hypotension, electrolyte disturbance.
interactions_checked.action: If dapagliflozin added, reassess thiazide dose and monitor weight, BP, electrolytes.

interactions_checked.interaction: Minimal CYP‑mediated interactions; safe with ACE‑I, statin, metformin, SGLT2‑i.

contraindications.reason: Contraindicated if eGFR <30 mL/min/1.73 m² (risk of lactic acidosis). Patient eGFR not available.
contraindications.alternative: Delay initiation until eGFR confirmed ≥30; if eGFR <30, consider DPP‑4 inhibitor.

contraindications.reason: Contraindicated if eGFR <45 mL/min/1.73 m² or recurrent genital/UTI. Patient eGFR and infection history unknown.
contraindications.alternative: Obtain renal function and infection history before starting; if unsuitable, omit SGLT2‑i.

treatment_summary: Start ramipril as first‑line ACE‑I for hypertension, add atorvastatin for dyslipidaemia, and initiate metformin MR for prediabetes after confirming renal function. Consider semaglutide for weight loss if lifestyle measures insufficient, and dapagliflozin for additional CV/renal protection once eGFR ≥45 mL/min/1.73 m² and infection risk are ruled out. Review and possibly discontinue hydrochlorothiazide after ACE‑I titration. All choices follow NICE CG181, NG136 and NG28 recommendations, with monitoring of BP, lipids, HbA1c, renal function, electrolytes, and CK as outlined.
